notes.text: Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow attackers to execute arbitrary commands or code remotely on affected systems.
notes.title: Advisory Summary

notes.text: Critical Manufacturing, Defense Industrial Base, Emergency Services, Transportation Systems
notes.title: Critical infrastructure sectors

notes.text: CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

notes.text: These vulnerabilities have a high attack complexity.
notes.title: Recommended Practices

All-Line Equipment Company Fuel-Boss V1 Backflush Systems: >=|<=PHP_7.1.5_7.1.5

cwe.name: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')

notes.text: Fuel-Boss is vulnerable to the University of Washington IMAP Toolkit 2007f on UNIX, used in imap_open() in PHP and other products, launching an rsh command via the imap_rimap and tcp_aopen functions without preventing argument injection, which can allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary OS commands when an untrusted IMAP server name is supplied and rsh has been replaced by a program with different argument semantics such as ssh. This enables attacks through IMAP server names containing a "-oProxyCommand" argument, as well as a stack-based buffer overflow that may allow an attacker to remotely execute arbitrary code.
notes.title: Vulnerability Summary

remediations.details: Fixes are available for the Fuel-Boss V1 Standard and Fuel-Boss V1 Portal. Please contact All-Line Equipment Company (866-356-3336) for instructions on how to receive these fixes.
Fixes are not yet available for the Fuel-Boss V1 Master/Slave.
No fix is planned for Fuel-Boss V1 Backflush Systems.
All-Line Equipment Company recommends either taking products that are not fixed off the Internet or restricting the IP addresses that can access them at the router level.

cwe.name: Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow')

notes.text: Fuel-Boss running versions up to and including PHP 7.1.5 is vulnerable because certain FPM configurations allow the FPM module to write past allocated buffers into space reserved for FCGI protocol data, thereby creating a possible remote code execution condition.
